cues.en: So I'm going to start with a question. Why haven't offline first apps taken off? The big problem with the web is that it does not work offline. And even if you are online, if you're on a slow internet connection, your app feels terrible. That sucks. Take a step back. That seems like a really big limitation of writing apps.
cues.zh: 我先从一个问题开始。为什么离线优先的应用没有流行起来？Web 最大的问题是它无法离线工作。即使你在线，如果网络连接很慢，你的应用体验也会非常糟糕。这很糟糕。退一步想，这似乎是编写应用的一个非常大的限制。

cues.en: So there's this idea where you write apps that work offline by taking offline into consideration from the very beginning. And what that really leads to is basically just writing a full local app. So the entire app's code and all of your data is completely local. That's really what it leads to, because to work offline and to boot it up offline, you kind of just have to do that. So it's a complete rearchitecture. And personally, I actually like the term local first apps better.
cues.zh: 所以有这样一个想法：你编写应用时，从一开始就把离线考虑进去，让应用能离线工作。这实际上基本上就是编写一个完整的本地应用。所以整个应用的代码和你的所有数据都完全在本地。这确实就是它的结果，因为要离线工作、离线启动，你基本上就得这么做。所以这是一次彻底的重构。就我个人而言，我其实更喜欢“本地优先应用”这个说法。

cues.en: So the main problem why I think they haven't taken off is because syncing is very, very hard. And if you're a full local app, you have to deal with syncing, where if you have these apps across devices, then you have to sync your data across the devices. And turns out, this is actually super, super hard. You cannot just queue up changes into an array when you're offline, and then when you come back online, push them out to the server. That does not work. So a lot of local apps, they...
cues.zh: 所以我认为它们没有流行起来的主要问题在于，同步非常非常难。而如果你是一个完整的本地应用，你就必须处理同步问题：如果你在多个设备上都有这些应用，那么你就必须在设备之间同步数据。而事实证明，这实际上超级超级难。你不能在离线时只是把变更排进一个数组，然后等重新上线时再把它们推送到服务器。那样行不通。所以很多本地应用，它们……

cues.en: say that they have offline support, but you always end up running into these situations. You're doing stuff offline, and then suddenly this big red scary box comes up and says, attempting to restore connection. Changes may now may not be saved. I mean, come on, why don't you just tell me they won't be saved? OK. So let's take a sit back. The first thing we need to do is we have to admit that local apps, they are a distributed system.
cues.zh: 声称自己有离线支持，但你最终总会遇到这些情况。你正在离线做事情，然后突然弹出一个红色的大警告框，说“正在尝试恢复连接。更改可能现在可能不会被保存。”我是说，拜托，你为什么不直接告诉我它们不会被保存？好吧。所以我们退一步。我们需要做的第一件事是，我们必须承认，本地应用是一个分布式系统。

cues.en: There's no way around that. We have multiple instances of your app on different devices, and they can go off and do their own thing, and then they need to come back and sync up. That is a distributed system, and distributed systems are very hard to get right. So, I am James Long. I did create prettier. A lot of other people helped push it to mainstream, so I'm very grateful for those.
cues.zh: 这一点无法回避。你的应用在多个设备上有多个实例，它们可以各自独立运行，然后需要回来同步。这就是一个分布式系统，而分布式系统非常难以做对。所以，我是James Long。我创建了prettier。还有很多其他人帮助将它推向主流，所以我非常感激他们。

cues.en: These people are. Recently, I've been working on an app called Actual. It's a personal finance app. You can go to actualbudget.com if you want to check it out. This is a full local app, but it seamlessly syncs across devices. So when I started Actual, these were my requirements. These were the features that I wanted to really have. It had to be available offline, and it had to be fast. It turns out when all of your data is local and it's just there all the time, you just end up getting a super fast app without much work.
cues.zh: 这些人就是。最近，我一直在开发一个叫Actual的应用。它是一个个人财务应用。你可以去actualbudget.com看看。这是一个完全本地的应用，但它能无缝地跨设备同步。所以当我开始做Actual时，这些是我的要求。这些是我真正想要拥有的功能。它必须能离线使用，而且必须快。事实证明，当你的所有数据都在本地，一直就在那里时，你最终会得到一个超快的应用，而且不需要太多工作。

cues.en: Focus on privacy, also one of the ability to provide arbitrary queries. All of this led me to just build a local app that felt way better than building a normal web app. So here's an example of doing arbitrary queries. This feature's not actually released yet. But if you have a couple years or just a little bit of your financial data, you can come in here and create a custom report. And it has a MongoDB-ish style syntax that just compiles down to a SQLite query. I'm essentially exposing SQLite directly to you.
cues.zh: 注重隐私，也是提供任意查询的能力之一。所有这些让我构建了一个本地应用，感觉比构建普通Web应用要好得多。这里是一个进行任意查询的例子。这个功能实际上还没有发布。但如果你有几年或一点点财务数据，你可以来这里创建一个自定义报告。它有一种类似MongoDB风格的语法，可以编译成SQLite查询。我本质上是在直接向你暴露SQLite。

cues.en: you would never ever do this if you were writing a cloud-based app. You would never imagine taking arbitrary code and executing it on your server, right? There's a reason why you don't do that. There's a reason why GraphQL doesn't even have a simple aggregate function like sum. Because all your data's local, sure, you can SQLite inject yourself as much as you want, whatever. So I realized, though, shoot, I need a mobile app, because you really do need to have your transactions on the go. So I was like, crap, I need to figure out syncing. So this led me down a whole path of, you know,
cues.zh: 如果你在写云端应用，绝不可能这么做。你绝不会想把任意代码拿到服务器上去执行，对吧？不这么做是有原因的。这也是为什么 GraphQL 连像 sum 这样简单的聚合函数都没有。但既然数据全在本地，当然，你爱怎么对自己搞 SQLite 注入都行，无所谓。但我随即意识到，糟了，我需要一个移动端 App，因为你确实得随时随地记账。于是我想，完蛋，我得搞定数据同步了。这让我走上了一条……

cues.en: building a sync engine, pretty much, for better or for worse, I stopped building a product, and I built my own sync engine. But I did launch my product, so at least there's that. So here's an example. You can fill in some budget values on one client. Of course, it can sync between desktop apps, too. So the second one syncs, and it got those budget values. It adds another one. And then this one also deletes a category. And then when the other one syncs up, so you can merge categories and do all this complicated stuff. The other one syncs up, and it has exactly the same state.
cues.zh: 差不多就是手搓同步引擎的路。不管好坏，我暂停了产品开发，自己写了一套同步引擎。不过我最后确实把产品发布了，至少这点还算欣慰。这里举个例子：你可以在一个客户端上填写一些预算数值。当然，桌面应用之间也可以同步。第二个客户端一同步，就拿到了那些预算值。接着它又加了一条。然后这边又删掉了一个分类。接着当另一个客户端同步时——你可以合并分类，做各种复杂的操作——另一个客户端同步完成，两边的状态就变得完全一致了。

cues.en: So these were my use cases. I have very simple data. We're talking about a 5-10 megabyte SQLite database. We're not building a back-end database that has to deal with a terabyte of data. This is a whole different world. Also, I had to have syncing on top of SQLite. I was not willing to switch databases. So if you wanted to use a couple of the other solutions out there, they require you to just trust them to take your data. I did not want to give up SQLite. It gives me sub...
cues.zh: 这就是我的使用场景。我的数据非常简单，也就 5 到 10 MB 大小的 SQLite 数据库。我们又不是在构建那种得处理 1 TB 数据的后端数据库，这完全是两码事。另外，我必须基于 SQLite 来实现同步，我不打算换数据库。市面上现有的其他几个方案，都需要你完全信任他们，把数据交给他们托管。我不想放弃 SQLite，它能给我带来亚……

cues.en: sub-millisecond read queries, which is absolutely amazing. It's a whole reason why the app is fast, so I was not willing to give it SQLite. The syncing has to be a layer on top of it. To this day, I still don't understand why everything is so bundled together. Okay, so why is syncing so hard? There are two main problems, unreliable ordering and conflicts. Whatever we do here, whatever we do to solve this, it has to work 100% of the time.
cues.zh: 亚毫秒级的读查询，确实非常惊艳。这是应用运行速度快的根本原因之一，所以我不愿意把它换成 SQLite。同步必须作为其上的一层来实现。直到今天，我还是不明白为什么这些东西要被如此紧密地捆绑在一起。好，那为什么同步这么难？主要有两个问题：顺序不可靠，以及冲突。无论我们在这里做什么，无论我们如何解决这个问题，都必须保证 100% 的可靠性。

cues.en: This has to be seamless. There can never be no data loss or no state of the app that gets into a case where it doesn't work. Because remember, this is a local app. You can't just refresh the tab. I'm accepting the responsibility that this is going to work 100% of the time. So let's talk about unreliable ordering. So say you have two devices or two clients, and they do changes over time. Let's just say that they are making setting properties of an object.
cues.zh: 这必须做到无缝衔接，绝不能丢失数据，也不能让应用状态进入无法正常工作的情况。因为要记住，这是一个本地应用，你不能直接刷新标签页。我愿意承担这个责任，确保它 100% 的可靠。下面我们来聊聊顺序不可靠的问题。假设你有两台设备，或者两个客户端，它们会随时间推移进行修改。比如说，它们都在修改某个对象的属性。

cues.en: We want to think about this as if it's one timeline, right? That there's a sequential order of events. The problem is, though, that we are distributed. We have two apps that are doing different things at different times, and when they try to sync up, they are going to receive the changes at different times. So, B, does not get A's changes directly when they happen. It's not like quantum computing or something like that. And so, as the changes are propagated, synced back and forth between the devices,
cues.zh: 我们希望把它看成一条时间线，对吧？也就是说，事件有一个顺序序列。但问题在于，我们是分布式的。两个应用在不同时间做着不同的事情，而当它们尝试同步时，接收到这些变更的时间也会不同。所以，B 不会在 A 做出变更的同时直接收到 A 的变更。这又不是什么量子计算之类的东西。于是，随着变更在设备之间来回传播和同步，

cues.en: it's going to get them in different order. And so we can't just naively mutate our data as we are seeing changes. Otherwise, the first client would apply A, C, D, and B, if you can read that. And then the second client would apply B, A, D, and C. So obviously, we can't do out-of-order mutations because the resulting state is going to be different.
cues.zh: 它们到达的顺序会不同。因此，我们不能在看到变更时就直接、简单地修改数据。否则，第一个客户端会按 A、C、D、B 的顺序应用变更，如果你能看懂这个顺序的话；而第二个客户端会按 B、A、D、C 的顺序应用。显然，我们不能按乱序进行修改，因为最终得到的状态会不同。

cues.en: Back end apps, or back end databases, they have this thing called strong consistency, and this requires a lot of coordination, and it's actually really complex, and a lot of them actually don't actually get it right. A recent trend is to do eventual consistency, and this is a technique where you embrace the fact that there are multiple timelines. You embrace the fact that you are a distributed system, you admit that, and then you find solutions that mesh well with that, instead of trying to go against that. So the idea here is, is there a way to where
cues.zh: 后端应用或后端数据库都有一种叫作强一致性的机制，这需要大量协调，实际上非常复杂，而且很多系统都没能正确实现。最近的一种趋势是采用最终一致性，这种技术接受这样一个事实：系统中存在多条时间线。你接受自己处于分布式系统中，承认这一点，然后寻找与之契合的解决方案，而不是试图与它对抗。所以这里的想法是，有没有办法做到：

cues.en: Even if we get the changes in different order, is there a way that we can still produce the same state on each device? So this is the problem. If we can solve this and we have eventual consistency, as long as every single client has seen the changes, the same changes, even if they're out of order, then they will have the same state. So that is our goal. That is what we want to achieve. So how do we solve unreliable ordering?
cues.zh: 即使我们以不同顺序收到这些变更，能不能仍然让每台设备最终得到相同的状态？这就是问题所在。如果我们能解决它并实现最终一致性，那么只要每个客户端都看到过相同的变更，即使顺序不同，它们最终也会拥有相同的状态。这就是我们的目标，也是我们想要实现的结果。那么，如何解决不可靠的顺序问题呢？

cues.en: We need to assign time stamps. This is the first thing that we need to do. To do this, we can go back to Einstein. Time is relative. It's only net worth depends upon what we do as it is passing. So we don't need like a date.now timestamp. Obviously, there's clocks are horrible when we can't actually rely on date.now. What we want is just some order of events. So we just want some relative order where when a change happens here, what changes has that device already seen?
cues.zh: 我们需要分配时间戳，这是首先要做的事。为此，我们可以回到 Einstein 的观点：时间是相对的，它的价值只取决于时间流逝时我们做了什么。所以我们不需要像 date.now 这样的时间戳。显然，时钟并不可靠，我们不能真正依赖 date.now。我们需要的只是事件之间的顺序。也就是说，我们只需要一种相对顺序：当某个变更在这里发生时，那台设备之前已经看到过哪些变更？

cues.en: That's what we really want. So you could think of a sequence ID 1234, but we obviously can't do this because this would rely on some sort of global sequence ID and require strong consistency, and we just can't do that. We need a way to do this per device. So to do that, you need a clock. And you need a special kind of clock. So there's a couple different types of clocks, like a vector clock. Unfortunately, I don't have time to actually explain how these clocks work.
cues.zh: 这正是我们真正想要的。你可以想象一个序列ID 1234，但显然不能这么做，因为这依赖于某种全局序列ID，并且需要强一致性，而我们做不到。我们需要一种按设备处理的方式。为此，你需要一个时钟，而且是一种特殊的时钟。时钟有几种不同类型，比如向量时钟。可惜我没时间详细解释这些时钟的工作原理。

cues.en: But there's a vector clock. There's another clock called a hybrid logical clock, which is HLC. This is the kind of clock that I use. It's a super interesting clock. And what these clocks do is they exist per device. This is not something that exists on some local or like on some centralized server that everybody tries to coordinate with. These are per device clocks. What they do is they generate timestamps that we can assign to each change. So, for example, this is what HLCs look like. HLCs are super cool because they can be serialized to just a normal string.
cues.zh: 但有向量时钟，还有另一种叫混合逻辑时钟，简称HLC。这就是我用的那种时钟，非常有意思。这些时钟是按设备存在的，不是存在于某个本地或集中式服务器上让所有人去协调。它们是每台设备各自的时钟。它们的作用是生成时间戳，我们可以把它赋给每次变更。比如，HLC长这样。HLC非常酷，因为它们可以序列化成普通字符串。

cues.en: Again, the timestamp can be any value. The vector clock is actually a vector of multiple entries and stuff like that. All that we care about is when you assign a timestamp to a change, the clock is smart enough to give us, us being the ephemeral, whoever is trying to sync, some data so that we can compare changes and say, did this change when it happened on this machine? Did it come after all of these other things that the machine has already seen? So it's just a relative ordering.
cues.zh: 再说一次，时间戳可以是任意值。向量时钟实际上是由多个条目组成的向量之类的结构。我们关心的只是：当你给一次变更赋予时间戳时，时钟足够智能，能给我们——也就是任何试图同步的一方——一些数据，让我们可以比较变更，判断这次变更发生在这台机器上时，是否在机器已经见过的所有其他事情之后。所以这只是一种相对排序。

cues.en: So this is an example. There's two changes. Set X to three. Set X to five. Set X to three has a later time stamp. So the HLC provided this time stamp for us. And so if we were doing a last write wins, then setting X to three would win, in this case, if we were applying both of these changes. So don't get chipped up by the fact that it looks like we're actually using a real date, like you see a real date in here. Hyperological clocks. There's a whole paper written about the algorithm. It's super interesting.
cues.zh: 这是一个例子。这里有两处变更。把 X 设为 3。把 X 设为 5。把 X 设为 3 的时间戳更晚。所以 HLC 给我们提供了这个时间戳。那么如果我们采用最后写入获胜，在这种情况下，如果同时应用这两处变更，把 X 设为 3 就会胜出。所以别被这里看起来像真实日期这件事搞糊涂了，比如你在这里看到真实日期。混合逻辑时钟。有一整篇论文讲这个算法，非常有意思。

cues.en: And I don't have time to fully explain it right now, but just trust that we have this string that we can say, is this string less than this other string? Then that's the timestamp that came before that string. And that's what HLCs enable you to do. Now, Dijkstra said, simplicity is a prerequisite for reliability. This is a complex problem. Distributed apps and distributed systems is a complex problem. And the way to have it reliable is to have a simple solution.
cues.zh: 我现在没时间完整解释它，但你可以相信，我们有这样一个字符串，可以判断：这个字符串是否小于另一个字符串？如果是，那就是排在那个字符串之前的时间戳。这就是 HLC 能让你做到的事。现在，Dijkstra 说过，简单性是可靠性的前提。这是一个复杂问题。分布式应用和分布式系统是一个复杂问题。要让它可靠，办法就是有一个简单的解决方案。

cues.en: Complex problems do not necessarily beget complex solutions. We want this to be super reliable, 100% reliable, in the face of terrible networks, in the face of you putting your phone down for two weeks, picking it back up, and then it syncs to all these complicated changes, right? It has to work 100% of the time. For this to happen, we have to have the least amount of code possible, and that is what is so good about hydrological clocks. This is the entire implementation of hydrological clocks. Zero dependencies here.
cues.zh: 复杂问题不一定非要带来复杂解决方案。我们希望它超级可靠，100% 可靠，即使面对糟糕的网络，即使你把手机放下两周再拿起来，然后它要同步所有这些复杂变更，对吧？它必须 100% 的时候都能工作。要做到这一点，我们必须让代码尽可能少，而这正是混合逻辑时钟如此出色的原因。这就是混合逻辑时钟的完整实现。这里零依赖。

cues.en: It's 256 lines of JavaScript, right? How cool is that? Seems like you could sit down and learn that in a weekend, right? I feel like that a lot of times, as developers, we overcomplicate things, we try to take on too much of the problem. Let's try to distill things down into a single problem and solve that in 256 lines of JavaScript with no dependencies, because dependencies suck.
cues.zh: 这只有256行JavaScript，对吧？多酷啊？感觉你周末坐下来就能学会，对吧？我觉得很多时候，作为开发者，我们把事情搞得太复杂了，总想一口气解决太多问题。不如试着把问题提炼成单一问题，然后用256行无依赖的JavaScript来解决它，因为依赖这东西太烦人了。

cues.en: All right, so we've solved sort of solved the ordering problem. So what about conflicts? There's nothing around the fact that two devices can go offline, set the same piece of data, and then come back online. So we haven't magically solved that somehow. Well, what do existing solutions do? They say, well, you've got to write manual conflict resolution code, right? And the only response to that, my opinion, is, you know, did you just have to go screw myself? I mean, I believe I did, Bob.
cues.zh: 好，我们算是解决了排序问题。那冲突呢？两个设备可以离线，设置同一份数据，然后重新上线，这个事实无法回避。我们并没有神奇地解决这个问题。那现有方案怎么做？它们说，你得手动写冲突解决代码，对吧？在我看来，唯一的回应就是：你这是不是让我自认倒霉？我是说，我觉得确实是，Bob。

cues.en: Because really, manual conflict resolution does not work. It's basically just issuing one of the hardest parts of this whole thing onto you. And as a developer, you are not going to write correct manual conflict resolvers. I'm not going to. And I think I'm smart. There's just too hard. There's way too many edge cases to resolve conflicts. And conflicts, dealing with conflicts is something you need to be thinking about while you are structuring and shaping your data.
cues.zh: 因为手动冲突解决根本行不通。它基本上就是把整件事里最难的部分之一甩给你。作为开发者，你写不出正确的手动冲突解决器。我也写不出。我还自认为挺聪明的。这太难了。解决冲突有太多的边缘情况。而且冲突这件事，你需要在设计和塑造数据结构的时候就开始考虑。

cues.en: It's not a post-processing step, it's not a post-step that after everything syncs up, and then you resolve the conflicts. So the question is, how do we resolve conflicts, then? There is an answer to this. It's this magical thing called CRDTs. Okay, okay, I know what you're thinking. We're not going to get into any math, we're not going to do any complex stuff. It's really not as hard as it seems. All it is is a partially ordered monoid in the category of endofunctors.

cues.zh: 你可能见过这些术语。它们都只是 CRDT 的实现。所以 CRDT 更像是个宽泛的术语。它们没有权威实现。它就是这样，你完全不用操心这些。它们只是具有某些属性的数据结构，确切说是两个属性。一是可交换，意思是应用变更的顺序无关紧要。二是幂等，意思是应用该变更多少次都无所谓。想一下这个。

cues.en: If it doesn't matter what order you apply changes and doesn't matter how many times you apply the change, you can essentially just throw changes over the wall.
